purpose: HL7 v2.5.1 composite-datatype component dictionary for NPHIES message construction and structural validation. Layer 1 is the HL7 v2.5.1 standard component layout (provenance "hl7-base"); layer 2 is the NPHIES overlay extracted from the Confluence spec (provenance "nphies-table" / "nphies-guidance"), every overlay item carrying a verbatim quote.

provenanceLegend.hl7-base: HL7 v2.5.1 Chapter 2A standard datatype definition. Authored from the standard, NOT extracted from the NPHIES Confluence space.
provenanceLegend.nphies-table: Extracted from a table in the NPHIES Confluence space (accepted-component sub-table, or a comma-separated per-component length cell).
provenanceLegend.nphies-guidance: Extracted from NPHIES Confluence guidance prose and mapped onto a base-layer component index.

readingRules: Component indexes are ALWAYS the HL7 v2.5.1 indexes. NPHIES sub-tables list only the components NPHIES accepts; they never re-number.
A comma-separated "length" cell is a per-component length list, aligned with the components the field guidance names in order - not with components 1..N.
Anything marked "uncertain": true is advisory. Do not raise a structural error on it.
CM and Varies have no fixed component layout and assert nothing.

segmentTerminator.name: Carriage return
segmentTerminator.note: Always <CR>. Never configurable. Golden ADT_sample03/04 use \r; ADT_sample08 uses \n only (see goldenValidation.notes).

fieldSeparator.name: Field Separator
fieldSeparator.note: MSH-1 IS the separator character itself; MSH-2 begins immediately after it.

truncationCharacter.name: Truncation Character
truncationCharacter.note: Optional 5th character, added in v2.5.1. NPHIES golden samples send only 4 characters (^~\&).

source.quote:
MSH.1 Field Separator: "Definition: This field contains the separator between the segment ID and the first real field, MSH-2 Encoding Characters. As such it serves as the separator and defines the character to be used as a separator for the rest of the message. Recommended value is “|”"
MSH.2 Encoding Characters: "Definition: This field contains five characters in the following order: the component separator, repetition separator, escape character, subcomponent separator, and truncation character. Recommended value is |^~\&|"

delimiters.specInconsistency: MSH.2 guidance says 'five characters' but the recommended value it gives ('^~\&') is FOUR. HL7 v2.5.1 makes the 5th (truncation) character optional. Emit 4; accept 4 or 5.

escapes.rule: The escape character (default \) delimits an escape sequence that ends with the same character. Escape ONLY inside data content, never the structural delimiters themselves.
emitterOrder: never escape the delimiters that carry structure
notEscaped: MSH-1 and MSH-2 themselves are never escaped - they declare the delimiters

goldenValidation.method: Each golden ADT .txt was tokenised with a real HL7 v2 parser (segment terminator -> field separator -> repetition separator -> component separator -> subcomponent separator), then each target field was mapped onto this dictionary component-by-component and index-by-index.

assertions.detail: PID.3 parses as CX.1 ID Number = 30511223344557, CX.2/CX.3 empty, CX.4 Assigning Authority = HD with CX.4.1 Namespace ID = HealthId, CX.4.2 Universal ID = 2.16.840.1.113883.3.3731.1.1.100.1, CX.4.3 Universal ID Type = ISO. This is exactly what the guidance rule (CX.4.2 fixed to 2.16.840.1.113883.3.3731.1.1.100.1, CX.4.3 fixed to ISO) predicts, and it confirms Assigning Authority sits at component 4, not component 3.

PV1.3 parses as PL.1 Point of Care = ME, PL.2 Room and PL.3 Bed empty, PL.4 Facility = HD with PL.4.1 Namespace ID = SENDO, PL.4.2 Universal ID = 15000000112233, PL.4.3 Universal ID Type = ISO. NPHIES Table 10.1 lists "Facility Universal ID" whose length cell reads "Participant NHIC Organization ID"; the golden value at PL.4.2 is 15000000112233, the same NHIC Organization ID that MSH-4 Sending Facility carries. Table 10.1 is therefore a SELECTION of PL components 1,2,3,4.2,7,8,9 - it skips PL.5 Location Status and PL.6 Person Location Type - and is NOT a 7-component re-numbering.

PV1.7 parses as XCN.1 ID Number = 00TEST1980, XCN.2 Family Name = Test, XCN.3 Given Name = Test, XCN.4 Second and Further Given Names = Test, XCN.5 Suffix empty, XCN.6 Prefix = DR., XCN.7 Degree and XCN.8 Source Table empty, XCN.9 Assigning Authority = HD with XCN.9.2 Universal ID = 2.16.840.1.113883.3.3731.1.2.1 and XCN.9.3 Universal ID Type = ISO, followed by four more empty components (XCN.10-13). The prefix "DR." landing on component 6 and the OID landing on component 9 confirm the full 23-component v2.5.1 XCN order; a 5-slot reading of NPHIES Table 9.1 would have put the Assigning Authority at component 5 and mis-parsed this message.

PD1.3 could NOT be validated: none of the three golden ADT samples (ADT_sample03, ADT_sample04, ADT_sample08) contains a PD1 segment. The XON component model and the PD1.3 guidance rules (ID Number, Assigning Authority Universal ID = 2.16.840.1.113883.3.3731.1.2.2) are carried on the base layer plus the Confluence quote alone, with no golden corroboration. NOTE: the guidance names "ID Number", which in HL7 v2.5.1 is XON.3 and is marked retained-for-backward-compatibility (superseded by XON.10 Organization Identifier); NPHIES clearly intends XON.3, but a strict v2.5.1 reader may expect XON.10.

notes.detail: MSH-2 literally contains '^~\\\\&' (5 chars). HL7 v2.5.1 requires '^~\&'. The message body nevertheless uses & as the subcomponent separator (e.g. PID.3 'HealthId&2.16...&ISO'), so the intended encoding characters are '^~\&' and this is a defect in the sample file, not a different encoding. Parsed with '^~\&'.

MSH-2 literally contains '^~\\\\&' (5 chars). HL7 v2.5.1 requires '^~\&'. The message body nevertheless uses & as the subcomponent separator (e.g. PID.3 'HealthId&2.16...&ISO'), so the intended encoding characters are '^~\&' and this is a defect in the sample file, not a different encoding. Parsed with '^~\&'.
ADT_sample08.txt uses bare LF as the segment terminator; ADT_sample03/04 use CR. HL7 v2.5.1 requires CR (0x0D). Parser accepted both.

PV1.3 is populated (ME^^^SENDO&15000000112233&ISO) in all three ADT samples, but the ORU page (171246311) marks PV1.3 usage 'I' (ignored). The ADT page (7766425) marks it 'O'. Usage is message-type specific; this dictionary asserts structure only, not usage.
